beats.trigger: When do you split, and how?
beats.got: A question I can use: is splitting worth the cost?

beats.trigger: A hundred tiny agents cost more to coordinate than they save.
beats.got: There is a cost to over-building. Still no number.

beats.trigger: If one agent can produce what you need, use one.
beats.got: The default is the cheap option, and splitting has to justify its coordination cost. That is how I judge any spend.

beats.trigger: A legal-policy agent shouldn't have customer-data access.
beats.got: Three tests for splitting: access, dialect, stance. Access is a control I understand, like segregation of duties.

beats.trigger: Split for a reason, not because "three is more thorough".
beats.got: More agents do not mean more rigour. This is understated, and I respect that.

beats.trigger: The synthesizer then commits to one diagnosis and drops what does not serve it.
beats.got: Without a framework it averages the views. With one it picks, and the dropped material is gone.

beats.trigger: Could one prompt produce the same quality of output?
beats.got: A test I can ask a vendor or my team: could one prompt do this? That is a reason to say no.

beats.trigger: Each helper gets one job, reports back as a file and disappears.
beats.got: Two ways to run several agents. I could not pick between them myself.

beats.trigger: An agent that works across connected systems has access to those systems.
beats.got: The right question is the worst case given the access. That is how I think about risk.

take_homes: Default to one agent. Splitting needs a reason and has a coordination cost.
Ask 'could one prompt do this?' before paying for a multi-agent setup.
Handoffs between agents are where numbers get dropped silently, and nothing in the module checks that the final answer is true.

monday.move: Ask the controller to try one agent on the month-end variance commentary, and have a person check every number in it.
monday.stop_condition: Any number in the commentary that does not tie to the ledger
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data.

misconception.why: The module is about how to build and fix agent systems, but it never gives a cost, a payback or a licence comparison. The 'one agent unless forced' point is sound. It did not move me from 'AI is a licence we buy' to a capability we build.

one_line: The best part was 'use one agent unless you can show why not'. The rest was a day of exercises with no cost per month and no figure for the board.
